statements.status_notes: CVE-2026-54875 ("Non-Constant-Time SM2 Scalar Multiplication on ARM64 and RISC-V", Low): on ARM64 and RISC-V, SM2 signing and decryption use an optimised scalar multiplication whose branches and table look-ups depend on the secret scalar, so an attacker who can measure timing or cache access can learn information about the private key. OpenSSL 3.5 is affected on AArch64 and RISC-V and fixed in OpenSSL 3.5.9; the FIPS module is not affected because SM2 is not a FIPS algorithm and the optimised SM2 code is not part of the FIPS module. https://openssl-library.org/news/secadv/20260929.txt, fix on the openssl-3.5 branch https://github.com/openssl/openssl/commit/469f3e42629f4a0b5631796e20c66c92c138a3e8, first released in OpenSSL 3.5.9. Debian fixed it for trixie in openssl 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 (DSA-6531-1, https://security-tracker.debian.org/tracker/CVE-2026-54875). The DHI Debian 13 openssl packages are rebuilds of Debian's trixie openssl, published in the DHI Debian repository and the DHI enterprise repository (the FIPS builds, and the openssl-provider-fips package of every build, only in the enterprise repository); the Debian changelog shipped in each libssl3t64 package shows which Debian release a build is based on. That changelog was read from every published build on amd64 and arm64: 25 versions, 17 standard and 8 FIPS builds, based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 and 3.5.9-1~deb13u1. No build based on Debian 3.5.5-1~deb13u2, 3.5.6-1~deb13u1, 3.5.6-1~deb13u2 or 3.5.7-1~deb13u2, FIPS builds included, names CVE-2026-54875. The first published rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3, the fixed boundary here, and every later build, FIPS builds included, carry Debian's 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 entry naming it. The optimised SM2 code is compiled only into the arm64 builds: the libcrypto debug symbols of the last rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u2 and the first rebuild of Debian 3.5.7-1~deb13u3 list EC_GFp_sm2p256_method and the ecp_sm2p256 point and field functions on arm64 and not on amd64; the range is published for both architectures, so the amd64 builds below the boundary read as affected although they do not contain that code. Of the FIPS providers, the openssl-provider-fips package, read from every build on both architectures, ships the OpenSSL 3.1.2 FIPS provider in the FIPS builds and the FIPS provider from the build's own OpenSSL release (3.5.5, 3.5.6, 3.5.7 or 3.5.9) in the other builds; the advisory places the affected code outside the FIPS module boundary, and the FIPS builds' libcrypto and libssl are Debian's 3.5 libraries checked above.
